`email.utils.parseaddr()` and `getaddresses()`, even in `strict=True` mode (the default since the CVE-2023-27043 fix), silently drop a comment that is embedded inside a dot-atom and splice the surrounding atoms together:

```python
>>> from email.utils import parseaddr
>>> parseaddr('u(comment)ser@d.com', strict=True)
('comment comment', 'user@d.com')
```

The strict parser rejects the same input:

```python
>>> from email.headerregistry import Address
>>> Address(addr_spec='u(comment)ser@d.com')
InvalidHeaderDefect: local-part is not dot-atom, quoted-string, or obs-local-part
```

So a caller that validates or authorizes with `parseaddr` and then hands the original string to a strict component gets a subject mismatch — the same class as CVE-2019-11340 and the motivation for CVE-2023-27043.

Proposal: in strict mode, fail closed (return `('', '')`) when a comment is embedded inside a dot-atom instead of splicing. `strict=False` would keep the historical lenient behavior. I'm happy to prepare a PR.

Reproduced on CPython 3.14.6.
